\section{Overview}
\subsection*{Brief: usb-buck (S14 run b)}
A 4-layer STM32 USB device board:

\begin{itemize}
\item STM32F103C8T6 MCU, 8 MHz crystal, SWD header (4-pin)
\item USB micro-B connector, USB 2.0 full-speed DEVICE on the MCU's USB pins
\item Powered from USB VBUS (5V) through an AP63203 buck converter to 3.3V
\item One status LED on a GPIO; one user button
\item JLCPCB 4-layer, economy PCBA, max 55x45 mm, prototype qty 10
\item Prefer JLC Basic parts; hand-solderable connectors acceptable
\item Structure the schematic hierarchically (e.g. power / mcu / usb sheets)
unless the architect judges flat clearly better
\end{itemize}

\section{Requirements}
\subsection*{Requirements: usb-buck}
\subsubsection*{1. Function}
USB-powered STM32 device board. STM32F103C8T6 MCU (clocked from an 8 MHz crystal) runs USB 2.0 full-speed device firmware, talking to a host over a micro-B USB connector that also supplies board power. Onboard status LED and user button give minimal local UI/debug feedback; a 4-pin SWD header supports programming and debugging. Compact prototype/dev board, build qty 10. Note: brief requests a hierarchical schematic (e.g. power/mcu/usb sheets) unless the architect judges a flat schematic clearly better - carried forward as a directive for the architecture stage, not a board requirement.

\subsubsection*{2. Interfaces}
\begin{itemize}
\item USB: USB 2.0 full-speed DEVICE (stated). Connector: micro-B (stated).
D+/D- wired to the MCU's fixed USB pins - PA11 (D-) / PA12 (D+) on the
STM32F103C8T6 (verified against part datasheet references). Device only:
no host, hub, or OTG function.
\item SWD: 4-pin header for programming/debug (stated). ASSUMED: standard
minimal SWD-only pinout - SWCLK, SWDIO, GND, 3V3 reference (no NRST, no
SWO); 2.54 mm pitch, unshrouded pin header. Low risk - architect picks
exact pin order and silkscreen labels it.
\item User I/O (onboard, no external connector):
\begin{itemize}
\item 1x status LED, GPIO-driven. ASSUMED: color/pin is architect's choice,
cosmetic only.
\item 1x user button, GPIO input. ASSUMED: generic application input (not
BOOT0/bootloader select, not NRST/reset) - brief calls it "user
button" distinctly from any programming function.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{3. Power}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source: USB VBUS only. No battery, no charging, no mains input.
\item Input: 5V nominal (USB spec range \textasciitilde{}4.75-5.25V). Budget: 500mA-class
(standard USB downstream port; no PD/QC negotiation implied or needed).
\item Regulation: AP63203 buck converter, VBUS (5V) -\textgreater{} 3.3V rail (stated,
named part). NOTE: this explicit part name overrides the general
"prefer JLC Basic parts" preference for this one IC; architect verifies
sourcing (JLC Basic/Extended/LCSC) and applies the Basic-parts
preference to every other part.
\item Rail budget (GUESS, for architect sizing only): MCU active \textasciitilde{}50mA, LED
\textasciitilde{}5-10mA, misc pull-ups/passives \textasciitilde{}5mA -\textgreater{} well under 150mA on the 3.3V
rail. Comfortably inside both the buck converter's and the USB port's
capability.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{4. Environment}
Not stated. ASSUMED: indoor bench/lab prototype use, ordinary room ambient (roughly 0-40C), no enclosure, no ingress protection, no vibration/shock requirement. Low risk - qty-10 prototype board, easy to revisit.

\subsection*{Sheet plan}
\subsection*{usb-buck - hierarchical sheet plan}
Three child sheets under a thin root, per the brief's request for a hierarchical schematic. The board has \textasciitilde{}28 components across three clearly separable domains and exactly TWO nets that cross a sheet boundary, so hierarchy costs almost nothing in net-name risk and buys parallel P4 sheet generation.

\textbf{The sheet NAMES below are contractual.} They appear verbatim in netlist net names (\texttt{/mcu/OSC\_IN}) and \texttt{constraints.json} already references them; renaming a sheet renames nets and breaks \texttt{netlist\_audit --constraints}.

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\textbar{} Sheet \textbar{} File \textbar{} Blocks \textbar{} Interface nets (sheet pins) \textbar{} pwr\_base \textbar{}\\
\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} root `usb-buck` \textbar{} `usb-buck.kicad\_sch` \textbar{} none (stitching only) \textbar{} - \textbar{} 1 (unused) \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `usb` \textbar{} `usb.kicad\_sch` \textbar{} USB port + ESD \textbar{} `USB\_DP`, `USB\_DM` \textbar{} 300 \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `power` \textbar{} `power.kicad\_sch` \textbar{} buck regulation \textbar{} {*}{*}none{*}{*} \textbar{} 100 \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `mcu` \textbar{} `mcu.kicad\_sch` \textbar{} MCU core + clock, user I/O, debug \textbar{} `USB\_DP`, `USB\_DM` \textbar{} 200 \textbar{}
\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{1. Net naming - the CANONICAL final netlist names}
Mechanism (verified in this repo: \texttt{tests/s7\_regen/hierdemo/kicad/hierdemo.net} produces \texttt{+3V3}, \texttt{GND}, \texttt{/VIN}, \texttt{/CTL}, \texttt{/load/LED\_K}):

1. \textbf{Power SYMBOLS make a net global across the whole hierarchy} with a BARE name and need NO sheet pin. 2. A child net merged with the root through a sheet pin takes the {*}{*}root-side label{*}{*}: \texttt{schlib.Project.add\_sheet(child, ..., nets={[}"X"{]})} wires each sheet pin outward to a root local label \texttt{X}, so the net becomes \texttt{/X}. 3. A child-internal label becomes \texttt{/\textless{}sheet\textgreater{}/NAME}.

\paragraph*{Global rails (power symbols, no sheet pins) - bare names}
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright

\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `VBUS` \textbar{} `power:VBUS` \textbar{} usb, power \textbar{} J1 pin 1 (passive) -\textgreater{} {*}{*}needs PWR\_FLAG{*}{*} \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `+3V3` \textbar{} `power:+3V3` \textbar{} power, mcu \textbar{} L1 pin 2 (passive - the AP63203 has no VOUT pin, the rail forms after the inductor) -\textgreater{} {*}{*}needs PWR\_FLAG{*}{*} \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `GND` \textbar{} `power:GND` \textbar{} all \textbar{} {*}{*}needs PWR\_FLAG{*}{*} \textbar{}
\end{quote}
All three PWR\_FLAGs live on the \texttt{power} sheet (\texttt{\#FLG0100}+). Power symbols being global, one flag each drives the net hierarchy-wide.

\item \textbf{J2 SWD}: 1 = +3V3 (reference OUT), 2 = SWCLK, 3 = GND, 4 = SWDIO. ST

\subsubsection*{4. U1 pin commitments (P4 wiring contract, LQFP-48)}
Pin numbers below are from the verified DS5319 pin table used by the stm32-blinky sheet plan plus the USB research (PA11 = 32, PA12 = 33); \textbf{P4 re-confirms every number against the `parts/` datasheet extract} before wiring - PB0's number in particular is not pinned here.

\begin{itemize}
\item VBAT (1) -\textgreater{} \texttt{+3V3} (no battery) + C18. VDD 24/36/48 -\textgreater{} \texttt{+3V3} + C12/C13/C14
+ C15 bulk. VDDA (9) -\textgreater{} \texttt{+3V3} + C16 + C17. VSS 23/35/47 -\textgreater{} \texttt{GND},
VSSA (8) -\textgreater{} \texttt{GND}.
\item PC13 (2) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/LED} (sink only; ST limits PC13-15 to 3 mA).
\item PD0/OSC\_IN (5) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/OSC\_IN}, PD1/OSC\_OUT (6) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/OSC\_OUT}.
\item NRST (7) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/NRST}.
\item PB0 -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/BTN} (active low; PA0/WKUP left free for a future active-high
wake-up function).
\item PA11 (32) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/USB\_DM}, PA12 (33) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/USB\_DP}. \textbf{No series resistors} -
the F103 PHY's output impedance is internal; 22R/33R would push it outside
the USB 28-44 ohm window.
\item PA13 (34) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/SWDIO}, PA14 (37) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/SWCLK} (SWD is the reset
default on these pins).
\item BOOT0 (44) -\textgreater{} \texttt{/mcu/BOOT0} -\textgreater{} R3 10 k -\textgreater{} GND (fixed strap; the user button
is explicitly NOT a boot selector).
\item PB2/BOOT1 (20) and every unused GPIO: no-connect flag so ERC is clean.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{5. P4 generator notes (schlib specifics that bite)}
1. \textbf{`power` sheet has no sheet pins}: `proj.add\_sheet(power\_sheet.build(), at=..., size=..., nets={[}{]})`. All three of its rails are power symbols and are global already. Do not invent sheet pins for rails. 2. \textbf{Use the free-cluster `hier\_pin(net, at=...)` variant} on both the \texttt{usb} and \texttt{mcu} sheets for \texttt{USB\_DP}/\texttt{USB\_DM}. Each net has 2+ components on it, and that variant places a LOCAL label plus the hierarchical label on one stub so the hier label joins by wire geometry rather than relying on hier-label/local-label name merging. 3. \textbf{Root-side labels sit 7.62 mm to the LEFT of each sheet pin} (add\_sheet's \texttt{label\_stub = 3 {*} STUB}), and sheet pins stack down the sheet symbol's LEFT edge. Leave that strip clear when placing the \texttt{usb} and \texttt{mcu} sheet symbols on the root, and give both sheets the same \texttt{nets=} order. 4. \textbf{PWR\_FLAGs}: \texttt{power\_flag("VBUS", sym="power:VBUS", flag=True)}, same for \texttt{+3V3} and \texttt{GND}, all on the \texttt{power} sheet. Without them ERC reports the rails as undriven (every driver on this board is a passive pin - connector, inductor). 5. \textbf{U3 in-line wiring}: the array's two same-channel I/O pads are internally common - wire BOTH pads of a channel to the same net so layout can pass the trace through the part with no stub. Its VBUS/supply pin ties to \texttt{VBUS}. Confirm the pin table from the P3 datasheet extract; do not wire from memory. 6. \textbf{Decoupling metadata}: rails on the \texttt{mcu} and \texttt{power} sheets are power symbols, so the wiring label and the final net name agree (\texttt{+3V3}, \texttt{GND}) and no \texttt{rail\_net}/\texttt{gnd\_net} override is needed anywhere on this board. 7. \texttt{Sheet.add\_component(..., expect=\{...\})} on U1, U2, U3 - pin-name insurance against a wrong symbol.

\subsubsection*{6. Board-edge placement (mirrors constraints.json)}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{J1 (micro-B) on the LEFT edge}, pos 0.5 - the plug must seat, and this
puts the pair's origin on the short axis with a straight shot to U1 in the
middle of the board (usbbuck4 golden precedent).
\item \textbf{J2 (SWD header) on the RIGHT edge}, pos 0.5 - opposite the USB cable so
a debug ribbon and a USB cable do not fight, and PA13/PA14 sit on the
LQFP's right flank.
\item \texttt{separation} pushes U2/L1 at least 8 mm from J1/U3, keeping the 1.1 MHz
switch node out of the corner where the USB pair starts.
\item \texttt{groups}: \texttt{xtal} (Y1 + C10/C11) and \texttt{buck} (U2 + L1 + C1-C5) so the
annealer moves each as a unit until P4's decoupling metadata takes over.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Design review of record}
\subsection*{Board review: usb-buck (adversarial, P8)}
Reviewer stance: machine gates are green (DRC 0/0 incl. warnings, verify 8/8 checks 0 findings, ERC 0/0); hunt only for what those checks cannot see. Evidence: fresh renders reports/renders/usb-buck\_\{top,bottom,iso\}.png at 2400 px plus close-up crops (crop\_usb.png, crop\_buck.png, crop\_u1.png, crop\_right.png, crop\_bottomui.png); SWIG geometry interrogation of kicad/usb-buck.kicad\_pcb (pads, tracks, vias, zones, silk inventory, collinear-overlap scan); requirements.md, architecture/{*}, constraints.json, reports/erc-waivers.md, reports/review-schematic.md, kicad/decoupling.json.

Verdict: 1 error, 4 warnings. The electrical design is delivered and the layout fundamentals (buck hot loop, ESD flow-through, plane discipline, decoupling ring) are genuinely good. The error and two of the warnings are "assembly/field reality" defects invisible to every script in the suite.

\subsubsection*{Findings, worst first}
\paragraph*{E1 - J2 SWD header has no silkscreen pin labels (error)}
The board's ONLY silk text is 28 refdes strings. requirements.md s2 promises the SWD pinout is "silkscreen label{[}ed{]}"; architecture/blocks.md (Debug) orders "Silkscreen every pin" and explains why: pin 1 carries +3V3 as a REFERENCE OUTPUT and "powering the board from the debugger would back-drive the buck output". As built (crop\_right.png), pin 1 is marked only by a square THT pad - invisible once the header is soldered - and nothing identifies SWCLK/GND/SWDIO. A user with a clone ST-Link (whose 3.3V pin SUPPLIES power) has a 50\% chance of connecting the ribbon reversed: SWDIO-\textgreater{}3V3 backfeeds the rail, debug fails, and the AP63203 output is back-driven. Minutes to fix (four silk labels + a pin-1 tick), and check\_silk can never see it - it checks geometry, not meaning.

\paragraph*{W1 - USB mouth recessed \textasciitilde{}0.5 mm behind the board edge (warning)}
J1's mating face sits at board x=11.0 vs edge x=10.54 (courtyard/silk front transformed from the footprint; no F.Fab body outline exists to be more precise). crop\_usb.png shows the PCB lip clearly in front of the connector mouth. A micro-B plug must insert \textasciitilde{}4.85 mm and compliant plugs expose \textasciitilde{}6.5 mm of shell, so \textasciitilde{}1.5 mm of slack absorbs this for most cables - but short-shell or chunky-overmold cables will bottom on the lip before the latch engages: intermittent contact, cable falls out. Standard practice is mouth flush to +0.5..1 mm proud. Shift J1 -0.5..-0.8 mm in x at the next spin (the placer respected courtyard-to-edge clearance where a connector wants overhang).

\paragraph*{W2 - J1 shield pegs and J2 leave JLC economy assembly unsoldered (warning)}
JLC economy PCBA is SMT-only. J2 (THT header) is planned as hand-solder per architecture - fine, bottom side is bare and access is excellent (usb-buck\_bottom.png). But J1's four shield legs are PTH pads (2x round 0.7 mm, 2x slot 1.3x0.5 mm, all net GND) and NO document calls out soldering them. Fresh from assembly, the shield-to-GND bond (decision 5) and nearly all of the jack's rip-off retention hang on unsoldered pegs in plated holes; the SMD signal pads alone will not survive cable side-loads for long. Failure: shield ground goes intermittent, then the jack tears off. Needs one line in the bring-up/assembly instructions: hand-solder J1's 4 pegs + J2's 4 pins. (The two 0.5 mm-wide slots sit exactly at JLC's minimum slot width - inside capability, zero margin; dfm\_check in S12 must confirm.)

\paragraph*{W3 - diff-pair constraint relaxation is defensible; its justification is flattering (warning)}
max\_uncoupled\_mm 5.0-\textgreater{}8.0 was corrected to pass the measured 6.61 mm uncoupled span. Geometry audit: the USBLC6-2SC6 traverse genuinely forces \textasciitilde{}3.4-3.6 mm of separation (GND pin 2 sits BETWEEN D-/D+ on the entry side; pads 1.9 mm apart \textgreater{} the 1.56 mm coupling window) - unavoidable with this part, as claimed. The "2.9 mm D+ pull-up stub" measures 3.16 mm junction-\textgreater{}R4.1, and \textasciitilde{}1.5 mm of it IS avoidable: R4's D+ pad is currently the FAR pad (y38.35); rotating R4 180 deg puts it at y36.85. Additionally the "coupled" remainder runs at 0.71-1.25 mm centre-to-centre against the 0.52 mm 90-ohm geometry (gap\_min 0.50 exists only near J1), so blocks.md's "90 ohm pair" is nominal, not delivered. Verdict: ACCEPT for USB full-speed - 12 Mbps / 4 ns edges over a \textasciitilde{}12 mm run above an unbroken In1 GND plane makes all of this immaterial (skew 1.93 mm = 13 ps is noise). Keep 8.0 mm for THIS board; do not let this constraints.json travel to any high-speed design, and drop the "zero avoidable meander" framing - R4's orientation was avoidable.

\paragraph*{W4 - D1 interior silk glyph contradicts the correct chamfer cathode cue (warning)}
LED-SMD\_L1.6-W0.8-R-RD footprint: the outline chamfer correctly marks the cathode end (pad 2, matches netlist - cathode to PC13 sink, anode via R1 to +3V3; crop\_bottomui.png), and it remains visible after assembly. But the interior glyph draws its polarity bar at local x=+0.09 with the tick toward -x - it reads as "cathode at the ANODE end". The glyph hides entirely under the 1.6 mm body once placed, so machine assembly (CPL-driven) and post- assembly inspection are safe. The exposure is hand-rework: with D1 removed, a tech who trusts the interior bar mounts the replacement backwards - LED dead (no damage, diode blocks). Low risk at qty 10; fix the glyph in the footprint at next touch. (fp\_verify's 0.8 vs 0.7 mm pad-size warning is a deliberate, benign enlargement - triaged, no action.)

\subsubsection*{Positively verified (not just "no finding")}
\begin{itemize}
\item ESD sequencing: J1 (x16.3) -\textgreater{} U3 (x19.1-21.4) -\textgreater{} U1 (x26.75); true
flow-through (entry/exit trace runs pad-to-pad under the SOT-23-6 body);
U3 GND drops to the In1 plane via at (18.45,34.25), 0.65 mm from pin 2 -
exactly the architecture's promise.
\item Buck hot loop (crop\_buck.png): C2 100nF 1.6 mm from VIN pin 3 with its GND
via 0.65 mm away; C1 10uF immediately behind; loop closes into In1 within
\textasciitilde{}2x2.5 mm. SW node is one 2.15 mm trace to L1 plus the 3.4 mm BST-cap leg -
tight and short for a 1.1 MHz sync buck. Output caps C4/C5 flank L1
symmetrically. C2 placement matches the layout note in blocks.md/power\_tree.
\item Planes: In1 = solid GND, In2 = +3V3, both filled, only 3 tracks on B.Cu
(SWDIO run, VBUS underpass) - the underpass's two vias sit 0.7 mm from the
D- line but two planes below it; return-path check (radius 2.0) green.
\item Crystal: Y1 (HC-49S) is 7.6+ mm from the buck bbox and \textgreater{}16 mm from edges;
load caps C10/C11 at the crystal pads with GND vias 0.65 mm out; OSC\_IN/
OSC\_OUT diverge immediately (no long parallel run); SWCLK passes no closer
than \textasciitilde{}1.3 mm north of the can. OSC traces are 11.9/12.6 mm - long-ish, the
price of the physically huge HC-49S; acceptable at 8 MHz over solid GND.
\item Placement contracts: J1/J2 on left/right edge at pos 0.5; buck group vs
USB group separation 9.8 mm (\textgreater{}= 8 required); board 50.1 x 40.1 mm inside
the 55 x 45 cap; single-sided SMT assembly delivered (bottom bare).
\item VBUS after P7 dedup: zero exact duplicates board-wide; VBUS itself also
free of partial overlaps. (22 micro-overlaps of 0.2-0.34 mm remain at
via junctions on GND/+3V3/D- - source-file cosmetics; copper unions in
gerbers, no fab impact.)
\item Pin-1 cues: silk dots present and post-assembly-visible for U1, U2, U3;
refdes all 1.0 mm, none obscured by parts (renders).
\item U1.8/U1.9 escape co-design at (36.3-36.4, 32.9-33.2): VSSA drops to plane
at (36.35,33.17), VDDA exits at y32.67 - 0.3 mm edge gap, no sliver.
\item Decoupling ring: C12/C13/C14 hug their VDD pins, C16+C17 on VDDA by pin 9,
C18 on VBAT, C15 bulk 6.6 mm off pin 48 (fine for bulk), C19 NRST cap
7.5 mm from pin 7 (filter still effective; cosmetic).
\item Cross-artifact: every requirements.md interface exists on copper (USB
device w/ ESD, SWD, LED, button, crystal, AP63203 buck); every blocks.md
block placed; VBUS carries exactly the "only capacitance allowed" set.
\end{itemize}
